newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Shin-Etsu unit plans T$7 bln Taiwan plant. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Shin-Etsu unit plans T$7 bln Taiwan plant. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects spelling of company name in headline.)
A venture controlled by Japan's Shin-Etsu Handotai Co Ltd said on Saturday it plans to invest T$7 billion in building its second silicon wafer plant in Taiwan's southern county of Tainan.

"Prospects for Taiwan's semiconductor industry is very good, so we plan to build our second plant to cope with rising demand for silicon wafers," Kuo Chih-hui, vice-president of Shin-Etsu Handotai (Taiwan), a venture 70 percent owned by Shin-Etsu Handotai and 30 percent by local partners, told Reuters.
Shin-Etsu Handotai, a silicon wafer manufacturer, is fully owned by Shin-Etsu Chemical, Kuo said by telephone.
Silicon wafer is the key material for making semiconductors.
The planned new plant will be located at Taiwan's second high-tech industrial zone in Tainan, which started construction in early 1996 with initial completion seen in 1998.

Shin-Etsu Handotai (Taiwan) plans to start building its second plant, with a monthly production capacity of 400,000 eigh-inch wafers, as early as late 1998, with completion seen one-and-a-half years later, Kuo said.
"But this is still a plan, which needs approval by our board meeting," he said.

The venture started building its first silicon wafer plant -- with a monthly capacity of 300,000 eight-inch wafers -- in March 1996 in Taiwan's first high-tech zone in the northern county of Hsinchu. The T$3 billion first plant is expected to start operations in July 1997, Kuo said.
Among the venture's local partners, Topco Scientific Co, the local agent for Shin-Etsu, has the main stake with an eight percent share, Kuo said. Kuo is also president of Topco.
The venture will be one of Taiwan's three silicon wafer makers.

The two others are Taisil Electronic Materials Corp, a venture of Taiwan's Asia Pacific Investment Co and Japan's Komatsu Electronics Metals Co Ltd, and a T$4.85 billion venture between China Steel and U.S.-based MEMC Electronic Materials.
Topco also plans to set up a new venture with Shin-Etsu Chemical to jointly invest T$3 billion in manufacturing quartz and other chemical raw materials in the Tainan industrial park, Kuo said.
